label: Being Reliable
framing: Reliability is faithfulness in the small thing, repeated until it becomes a character. Scripture promises that the one who is faithful in little is given much, and it does not ask for brilliance, only for a person who does what he said he would do, when he said he would do it. Most trust is not won by a grand act. It is built quietly, by being there, again and again.
cultural: The ancient economy ran on the steady worker and the honest weight far more than on the rare genius, and the parables Jesus told are full of stewards judged not by their talent but by their faithfulness. Our culture prizes the dramatic over the dependable, the launch over the maintenance, and so it is surprised when the flashy thing collapses and the boring, faithful thing is still standing. We have made consistency seem small. It is not small.
historical: Benedict of Nursia, in the sixth century, built a way of life around stability, the vow to stay and keep at it, against the restless monks who drifted from place to place. The whole of monastic culture, which preserved learning and faith through the collapse of an empire, rested not on heroics but on the daily return to the same work and the same prayers. Faithfulness, repeated for a lifetime, turned out to carry civilizations.
application: Do the small things you committed to, on time, even when no one is watching and no one would notice the lapse, because that is precisely where character is made. When you say you will be somewhere, be there, and when you cannot, tell them before, not after. Build a margin into your time so that one delay does not cascade into broken word. And measure yourself not by your best day but by your ordinary Tuesday.

verses.text: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.
Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,
